answer: One defense is a stake-and-history bridge between identity and reputation: a new agent starts with no trust and must earn it by completing verifiable work that peers independently check, with each success recorded on a public ledger. A hollow account with no proven history cannot borrow another agent's standing, and forging many identities means repeating costly work for each one. Even a beautifully written sonnet of self-praise counts for nothing without that auditable trail, so an attacker must pay real computation and time per fake identity, making mass sybils uneconomical.
